title: A scene can close its loop and still jerk
idea: Scrub a synthetic Gaussian scene under Fourier-periodic, endpoint-only and drifting motion. Inspect analytic position/velocity seam errors separately from camera closure.
controls: Phase, harmonics, period, deformation mode, camera path/orbit; PNG/GIF export in square or wide format.
misconception: Matching the first and last rendered frames does not ensure a smooth 3D loop; a mathematically closed loop can still move implausibly.
connection: OuroWorld · 8 Oct 2026. Implemented analytic teaching lab; not OuroWorld inference, learned deformation or an evaluation.

title: Separate tracks without changing the original mix
idea: Show two captioned stem streams and a protected mix as an attention matrix. Toggle the forbidden stem-to-mix edge and mix-token LoRA gate, tracing how information could alter the scene stream.
controls: Attention edges, stem-only adapter gate, per-stem captions, aligned versus concatenated time positions, clean versus noisy mix conditioning.
misconception: Blocking an attention edge alone does not freeze a stream if shared adapter updates still alter its token projections.
connection: SepGen · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed synthetic token calculation; no claimed audio separation score or generated waveform. Actual source timing and audio quality need the model.
audience: Audio/video model engineers and creative technologists

title: Why moving noise makes it fade
idea: Track a pixel footprint across a seeded noise grid. Compare ordinary averaging with variance-normalized projection; show histogram and cross-frame correlation.
controls: Zoom, footprint shape, camera motion, sample count, histogram bins, normalization; propose PNG/GIF/MP4 exports.
misconception: Warping standard Gaussian noise does not automatically preserve its variance. Unit variance also does not imply independent pixels.
connection: Tabula Rasa · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed analytic teaching model, not its renderer or generated footage.

title: An edit needs two scorecards
idea: Manipulate a synthetic scene and soundtrack. Plot intended change versus collateral change, then compare arithmetic and harmonic scoring.
controls: Object edit, background drift, sound timing, preservation, judge uncertainty; propose PNG/GIF exports.
misconception: An unchanged clip preserves everything but performs no edit; a convincing new clip can ignore preservation.
connection: CrossEdit · 7 Oct 2026. Proposed synthetic illustration of editing evaluation; no model output or reproduced benchmark.

title: The future you can still change
idea: Animate user and assistant token lanes, separating played audio from tentative future frames. Trigger an interruption and inspect discarded predictions and compute calls.
controls: Prediction horizon, confidence threshold, interruption timing, Listen/Speak policy; propose PNG/GIF exports.
misconception: Fewer model calls do not necessarily mean lower response latency or unchanged speech quality.
connection: DiffuPlex · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed scheduling schematic; synthetic tokens and timing, not a speech-model reproduction.

title: Shared references are guidance, not a guarantee
idea: Use a synthetic three-shot storyboard to show how a shared palette, character descriptor and reference bank reach each generation. Toggle shared versus per-shot inputs and display the exact conditioning each shot receives. Illustrative output swatches must be labeled as schematic, not vendor generations.
controls: Share reference bank; change one reference; per-shot override; guidance-strength schematic; reveal conditioning inputs; compare palette and identity labels across shots.
misconception: Saving a brand kit does not impose a hard mathematical identity constraint or guarantee every generated frame follows it. Shared inputs reduce one source of variation; model behavior remains a separate question.
connection: ElevenCreative Brand Kit, published 9 October 2026 and updated 12 October. Visual assets/rules are available across its image/video workflows; voice and sound are future work.
audience: Creative teams and ML practitioners designing multi-shot workflows
status: Proposed; no model outputs or consistency scores implemented
recommendation: A useful follow-up to the 3D consistency lab. Teach the difference between common conditioning and enforced invariants; do not simulate a vendor quality benchmark.

title: A preset needs a provenance trail
idea: Build a small visual dependency graph from reference assets through preset, model configuration, edits and export. Replay a deterministic toy transformation while selectively changing a dependency, so the viewer can see which outputs must be recomputed and why a seed alone cannot identify a complete workflow.
controls: Pin or change preset revision; swap reference asset; hold seed fixed; change model-version label; reveal dependency hashes; replay saved manifest; highlight affected descendants.
misconception: A seed or a named preset is enough to reproduce an output. Reproduction also depends on inputs, versions, settings and execution behavior; complete provenance still cannot guarantee deterministic external services.
connection: Higgsfield Katana released 8 October 2026, with a 12 October guide, brings reference-driven presets to Claude/MCP. Ad Multiplier gained a visual workflow on 6 October. Both make reusable workflows a timely topic; no claim that either currently provides this proposed provenance interface.
audience: AI filmmakers, creative technologists and pipeline engineers
status: Proposed; deterministic teaching graph only, no live vendor integration
recommendation: Keep the visual concrete: one changed reference should light up the affected shots. Show a compact export manifest rather than presenting a generic agent diagram.
